End-user requires native PyArrow struct field extraction capability in pandas Series to eliminate manual conversion overhead, maintain type safety, and improve workflow efficiency for hierarchical data analysis without sacrificing columnar performance benefits.

End users need efficient, type-preserving field extraction from PyArrow struct Series using intuitive accessor patterns to eliminate manual workarounds and maintain PyArrow performance benefits in data workflows.

Clarification needed on API design (accessor syntax and method signatures), nested struct handling, return type specifications, performance expectations, multi-field extraction support, null value semantics, and integration scope with pandas' indexing architecture.

Chain-of-thought reveals the core tension: balancing pandas' intuitive accessor patterns with PyArrow's type safety, and determining whether v1 should support complex scenarios (nesting, type coercion, bulk selection) or focus on single-field extraction MVP.

EndUser confirms core requirement: add intuitive field extraction for ArrowDtype(struct) Series via pandas accessor pattern (series.struct.field_name), maintaining type safety and PyArrow performance. API design must follow pandas conventions while addressing workflow friction from current manual extraction workarounds.

End user requirement for PyArrow struct field extraction in pandas is validated as new functionality addition. Core API should use series.struct.field_name accessor pattern preserving ArrowDtype. End-user requirements validated and refined: pandas needs new ArrowDtype(struct) field extraction feature using series.struct.field_name accessor syntax. All requirements traced to interview statements IR-PANDAS-001 through IR-PANDAS-006 and validated end-user confirmations.

No unresolved functional or non-functional gaps remain.
